title: Differential Equations for Living & Engineered Systems
description: Build, solve, and interpret first- and second-order differential equations, coupled systems, stability, and numerical integration for biological and robotic dynamics.

modifications: Linked the four original lesson pairs to the course outcomes: first-order solution methods to outcome 1, equilibrium and mechanical response to outcome 2, local linearization and stability to outcome 2, and Euler stability and accuracy to outcome 4. Clarified the damping-ratio objective, reassociated the preserved coupled-system stability item with its eigenvalue objective, and added direct formative checks for damping regime and local linearization; existing numeric prompts and keys remain unchanged.

Added an original Laplace-transform initial-value lesson with shifted-step forcing, partial-fraction practice and direct solution checks; reorganized the proposed 14-week sequence and combined related logistic readings in one week without claiming measured workload or semester equivalence.

Extended the existing forced-first-order lesson with an original Fourier-series example for a synthetic periodic input, harmonic-by-harmonic filtering, convergence limits and four formative checks. The 14-week schedule remains unchanged and the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

outcomes.description: Classify ODEs and choose solution methods.
Interpret equilibria, time constants, and stability.
Model coupled state variables as a vector system.
Check numerical solutions against physical constraints.

lesson_objectives.description: Solve separable and linear first-order ODEs.
Interpret equilibrium and characteristic time.
Relate natural frequency and damping ratio to qualitative transient behavior.
Write a mechanical model from force balance.
Linearize a nonlinear system near an equilibrium.
Use eigenvalues to classify local stability.
Apply forward Euler and recognize its limitations.
Choose a step size based on stability and accuracy, not convenience alone.
Derive a first-order linear ODE for a well-mixed chamber from a mass balance and classify it.
Compute the steady state, the time constant and the time to reach 90% of steady state.
Apply Euler's method, compare a step with the exact solution, and use the stability limit to check a numerical result against physical constraints.
Find the equilibria of a one-variable nonlinear ODE and classify their stability from the sign of the derivative.
Interpret the linearized slope at a stable equilibrium as a recovery time constant and find the harvest rate that maximizes sustained yield.
Write two coupled compartments as a matrix system and use its eigenvalues to determine stability and the slow and fast time scales.
Write the chamber equation for a time-varying feed and solve it by an integrating factor.
Compute the response to a step, a ramp, a sinusoid and a decaying input, including the lag and attenuation.
Use linearity to build the response to a pulse and to interpret how long a feed change takes to reach the culture.
Resolve a simple periodic feed into Fourier harmonics and combine their first-order steady-state responses.
Solve the free second-order equation and compute the natural frequency, damping ratio and damped period.
Use the logarithmic decrement to relate decay to damping, and the amplitude of successive oscillations.
Compute the steady-state amplitude of the forced oscillation across frequency and evaluate the resonance and its bandwidth.
Classify the equilibrium of x′ = A x from the trace and determinant of A.
Compute eigenvalues, eigenvectors and the constants of the solution for a given initial condition.
Interpret the behavior of a node, a spiral and a saddle, including the period and decay of a spiral.
Solve the logistic equation by separation of variables and evaluate the solution at a given time.
Compute the half-capacity time, the fraction of capacity reached, the early doubling time and the maximum growth rate.
Fit the growth rate from two counts by a logit transformation and quantify the error of an exponential extrapolation.
Find the steady states of a two-variable nonlinear system, including the symmetric one, and write the Jacobian there.
Compute the eigenvalues of the Jacobian and interpret a positive one as an instability and a negative one as a relaxation rate.
Explain bistability, and how a parameter crossing a threshold creates two stable states.
Compute the stability and positivity limits of explicit Euler and the amplification factors of explicit and implicit Euler for a decay equation.
Measure the stiffness of a linear system from its eigenvalues and estimate the number of steps a stable explicit method needs.
Solve a Michaelis–Menten depletion for the time to reach a concentration, and use it to judge a numerical result.
Summarize replicate counts by time and fit a straight line and a first-order decay to the early window.
Use each fitted model to predict later times and compare the predictions with the observed means.
Evaluate what the later observations say about the structure of each model and what validation would have shown it.
Distinguish a model-structure error from a numerical error as the cause of an impossible prediction.
Compute where a straight-line model crosses zero, the step-size limits of explicit Euler for a decay, and the results of Euler steps of different sizes.
Design validation that reveals the failure early: hold-out prediction, step refinement, independent data and invariant checks.
Transform first and second derivatives while retaining the initial values.
Solve a constant-coefficient initial-value problem by algebra and partial fractions, then check it in the original equation.
Represent a delayed step input and verify the response initial conditions and continuity at the delay.
Represent an impulsive input with the delta function, find the unit impulse response of a first- or second-order constant-coefficient equation, and interpret an impulse as a velocity jump.
Compute a response from rest as the convolution of the impulse response with the input, and check it with the convolution theorem.
Form the transfer function, judge stability from its poles, and compute the gain, phase lag and peak-gain frequency of the steady sinusoidal response.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week sequence only, not a measured or reviewed semester. It covers first- and second-order methods, adds bounded Laplace initial-value and impulse-response/convolution/transfer-function units in one week after constant-coefficient response, groups related logistic equilibrium and solution readings in one week, and ends with a synthetic-data lab and a validation case. All activities are open, ungraded practice; there are no graded homework sets, exams or project, and workload has not been measured, so the sequence is not evidence of semester equivalence.

weeks.title: A well-mixed perfused chamber: steady state, time constants and Euler stability
Forced first-order systems: steps, ramps, sinusoids and decaying inputs
Resonance and damping: free decay and forced oscillation

lessons.title: First-order models and time constants
lessons.worked_example: For ẋ=−0.25x with x(0)=8, the time constant is 4 time units and x(4)=8e^(−1)≈2.94, leaving 36.8% of the initial distance to equilibrium. For ẋ=−0.5(x−4) in seconds, τ=2 s and a start at 10 gives x(2)≈6.21.

lessons.title: A well-mixed perfused chamber: first-order linear ODEs, steady state, time constants and a numerical check
lessons.worked_example: With D = 0.05 and k = 0.02 min⁻¹, C_ss = 7.14 mM, τ = 14.3 min and 90% is reached at 32.9 min; one Euler step of 10 min gives 5.00 mM against the exact 3.60 mM, and steps above 28.6 min diverge.

modules.title: Forced first-order systems and periodic harmonic response

lessons.title: Forced first-order systems: steps, ramps, periodic inputs and decaying inputs in a perfused chamber
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic chamber of 15 mL perfused at 0.4 mL/min has τ = 37.5 min, reaches 0.7364 of a feed step after 50 min, and attenuates a 90 min cycle to 0.3568 with a lag of 17.3 min. For an ideal square-wave input of amplitude 1 mM, period 120 min and τ = 40 min, the first harmonic is attenuated to about 0.549 mM and the third to 0.0667 mM; in the earlier step example, the same 20 mL chamber reaches 95% in 119.8 min.

lessons.title: Second-order systems and mechanical response
lessons.worked_example: For m=2 kg, k=50 N/m and c=3 N·s/m, the natural angular frequency is 5 rad/s and the damping ratio is 0.15, so the transient oscillates at about 4.94 rad/s with a decaying envelope. Initial displacement and velocity determine its amplitude and phase.

lessons.title: Resonance and damping: free decay and forced oscillation of a spring–mass–damper
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic mount with m 0.05 kg, k 20 N/m and c 0.4 N·s/m has ωn 20 rad/s, ζ 0.2, a log decrement of 1.2825 and a resonant amplitude of 25.0 mm (Q 2.5) under 0.2 N; in the lesson, a pan with ζ 0.15 rings down to 0.0573 of its peak after three cycles and responds 20.8 mm at resonance.

lessons.title: Laplace transforms for initial-value problems: initial data and delayed steps
lessons.worked_example: For x'' + 3x' + 2x = H(t−2) from rest, X(s) = e^(−2s)/[s(s+1)(s+2)] and x(t) = H(t−2)[1/2 − e^(−(t−2)) + e^(−2(t−2))/2]; displacement and velocity are continuous at the switch, and substitution gives unit forcing afterward.

modules.title: Impulse response, convolution and transfer functions

lessons.title: Impulse response, convolution and transfer functions
lessons.worked_example: For x″ + 2x′ + 10x = f from rest, W(s) = 1/((s + 1)² + 9) has poles −1 ± 3i, so the system is stable and w(t) = (1/3)e^(−t) sin 3t, giving w(0.5) = 0.2017. At ω = 3, p(3i) = 1 + 6i gives gain 0.1644 and lag 80.5°; the gain peaks at ω_r = √8 = 2.828 with value 1/6.

lessons.title: Coupled systems, equilibria, and stability
lessons.worked_example: For J=[[0,1],[-2,-3]], the characteristic polynomial factors as (λ+1)(λ+2), so both local modes decay with time constants 1 and 0.5 time units. By contrast, eigenvalues −2 and +0.1 include a growing mode and make the equilibrium unstable.

lessons.title: Phase portraits of linear systems: eigenvalues, eigenvectors and the shape of the flow
lessons.worked_example: A system with A = [[−3, 2], [1, −2]] has trace −5 and determinant 4 (a stable node with eigenvalues −1 and −4), and from x(0) = (1, 2) it reaches (0.9207, 1.0560) at t = 0.5; in the lesson, the spiral with eigenvalues −0.5 ± 2j has a period of 3.1416 and shrinks by 0.2079 per turn.

lessons.title: Equilibria and stability: harvesting a logistic population and two coupled compartments
lessons.worked_example: With r = 0.03, K = 10⁶ and h = 0.01, N* = 6.667×10⁵ cells, recovery τ = 50 h and maximum sustained yield rK/4 = 7500 cells/h; the two-compartment matrix has eigenvalues -0.0354 and -0.5646 h⁻¹, both negative, so it is stable.

lessons.title: Logistic growth: the exact solution, fitting from data and the risk of extrapolating
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic culture with K 5 million, N₀ 0.1 million and r 0.08 h⁻¹ reaches half capacity at 48.6 h, holds 1.333 million at 36 h and doubles every 8.66 h early on, and an exponential forecast of 31.7 million at 72 h compares with a logistic 4.33 million; in the lesson, the culture with K 8 million has half capacity at 73.3 h and an exponential overestimate of 3.45 million at 72 h.

lessons.title: Nonlinear systems and linearization: a two-gene toggle switch and bistability
lessons.worked_example: For the toggle switch with a = 4, the symmetric state s = 1.3788 has m = 1.3106 and a positive eigenvalue 0.3106 (a saddle), and the stable asymmetric states are x = 3.7321, y = 0.2679 and the mirror image; in the lesson, a = 3 gives s = 1.2134, a positive eigenvalue 0.1911 and stable states (2.6180, 0.3820) and its mirror image.

lessons.title: Numerical ODEs and error control
lessons.worked_example: For y′=−50y, explicit Euler multiplies each step by 1−50h. The strict decay interval is 0<h<0.04 s; the boundary answer 0.04 s has factor −1 and does not decay. Nonnegative steps require h≤0.02 s. For x′=2, x₀=3 and h=0.25, one Euler step gives 3.5.

lessons.title: Stiff equations and implicit methods: stability limits of explicit Euler and the Michaelis–Menten depletion time
lessons.worked_example: For y′ = −20y with h 0.08 h, explicit Euler has factor −0.6 (stable but sign-flipping; limits 0.10 and 0.05 h), implicit Euler 0.3846 and the exact step 0.2019, and a substrate with V_max 1.5, K_m 0.8 falls from 4 to 0.4 in 3.628 h; in the lesson, λ 50 h⁻¹ gives a stability limit of 0.04 h and a depletion time of 2.826 h.

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: fitting decay models to a time course and testing them beyond the window
lessons.worked_example: In the synthetic cell counts the first-order decay fitted over 0 to 24 h has k 0.0676 h⁻¹, the straight line reaches zero at 27.5 h and predicts −66.9 at 48 h, and the first-order prediction of 3.79 at 48 h is 2.11 times lower than the observed 8.0.

lessons.title: When a fitted population model predicts negative counts: model structure, extrapolation, step size and validation
lessons.worked_example: For a second synthetic time course (N₀ 80, k 0.05 h⁻¹), the fitted line reaches zero at 32.8 h and predicts −35.2 at 48 h, a single 48 h Euler step gives −33.7 against an exact 2.19, and a hold-out fit predicts 6.9 at 24 h against an observed 24.1; in the lesson, the line for N₀ 100 and k 0.04 reaches zero at 37.6 h.

grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added two original lessons (a well-mixed perfused chamber with Euler stability; equilibria and stability of a harvested population and two coupled compartments) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a common-mistakes section to 1 original lesson that lacked one (differential-equations-5); each bullet names a mistake that the lesson's own text addresses. Fixed number formatting that an earlier authoring step left in learner-visible text: raw exponent notation (a number written with the letter e and a power of ten) and floating-point artifacts (a decimal with a long run of trailing digits) in the equilibria reading. No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a proposed 14-week schedule; seven original lessons (forced first-order systems in a perfused chamber; resonance and damping of a spring-mass-damper; phase portraits of linear systems; the exact solution, fitting and extrapolation of logistic growth; linearization and bistability in a toggle switch; stiff equations and implicit methods; and a fitted model that predicts negative counts, which prepares the course case on model structure, step size and validation); and a synthetic-data lab on fitting decay models. No new references were added. All activities remain ungraded practice; the package remains partial and unreviewed, gives no experimental protocol or parameter values for any real organism, and makes no claim about any culture or device.

Clarified three explicit Euler practice prompts and their feedback: the boundary permits zero, so they ask for a nonnegative result rather than a strictly positive one. Scoped the resonance statements item to the lesson's lightly damped, directly forced system. No answer key, tolerance, objective or option order changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-1 first-order reading with a separation-based solution, the integrating-factor form for linear equations, initial-condition role, equilibrium stability, time-constant interpretation and unit checks. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Three compact prototype readings remain in weeks 4, 6 and 11; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-4 mechanical-response reading with a signed force-balance derivation, natural frequency and damping ratio, transient classifications, initial-condition roles and a forced-response qualification. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Two compact prototype readings remain in weeks 6 and 11; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-6 coupled-systems reading with equilibrium linearization, Jacobian/eigenvalue interpretation, nullclines, local stability classifications and limits for nonhyperbolic or global conclusions. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. One compact prototype reading remains in week 11; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-11 numerical-methods reading with the forward-Euler derivation, stability versus accuracy, strict decay and positivity bounds, step refinement, and stiff-system considerations. Clarified the Euler practice prompt to ask for the stability boundary; its 0.04 s key, other keys and objectives are unchanged. All four original compact prototype readings now have expanded instruction; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Linked the first four lesson pairs to outcomes 1, 2 and 4. Clarified the damping-ratio objective, reassociated the preserved eigenvalue-stability item with its matching objective, and added direct formative practice for damping regime and local linearization; existing numerical prompts and keys remain unchanged. All four original compact readings remain expanded, and the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an inactive paper project for a normalized stiff two-compartment system, with an exact solution and peak, eigenvalue stability and positivity bounds, and explicit-versus-implicit Euler comparisons. The draft is ungraded and unreviewed; the package remains partial and formative-only.

Added original Laplace-transform IVP instruction with initial-value terms, partial fractions, delayed steps and direct checks. Reordered the proposed sequence and combined related logistic readings in one week; workload remains unmeasured, and the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Corrected the proposed 14-week schedule so every lesson_ids and assessment_ids field uses the required array shape after grouping the two related logistic readings. No new instruction or assessment was added; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Extended the existing forced-first-order lesson with Fourier-series decomposition of a synthetic square-wave input, harmonic-specific attenuation and phase, and limits near discontinuities. Four formative questions and three cards support the new objective; the schedule remains 14 weeks and the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Grouped an original impulse-response, convolution and transfer-function reading with the week-6 Laplace lesson: the delta function and velocity jumps, first- and second-order impulse responses, convolution from rest and the convolution theorem, poles and stability, and steady sinusoidal gain, phase and peak-gain frequency. Added three objectives, eleven formative items and four cards, with no week added, and pointed the Laplace lesson limits at the companion reading. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: The four former compact legacy readings now have expanded instruction beside the other content, and bounded Laplace initial-value and impulse/convolution/transfer-function units have been added. The package remains partial and is not equivalent to a full university semester.

A proposed 14-week schedule exists but is unmeasured and unreviewed. There is one synthetic-data virtual lab and no substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm or cumulative final. An inactive integrative project draft is not scheduled or graded.

Most practice items are short formative checks; the two transform units have six and eleven checks but does not replace a substantive homework sequence or demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery. Objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.

Of the 88 numerical answers in this package, 27 require a unit, one checks significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.

All populations, chambers, systems and numbers are synthetic teaching examples; this package gives no experimental protocols, parameter values for any real organism or process, or safety advice and says nothing about any real culture or device. The models are simplified textbook descriptions, not fitted models of real data.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, an activated integrative project and a laboratory sequence are not authored yet (one synthetic-data virtual lab exists); the original lessons extend a partial package.
